newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end range-trade mostly weaker.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end range-trade mostly weaker.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished another day of fairly light-volume trading mostly weaker.
Traders said most units again traversed well-worn ranges even during the session's most lively move sparked by a rumor that Russian president Boris Yeltsin had died.
That midday rumor was quickly denied when a Yeltsin press spokesman said Yeltsin was working at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow and was in satisfactory condition.
The rumor initially prompted a spike up to the day's peaks in most units, particularly the safe-haven Swiss franc, before the denial halted the buying and futures eroded again.

"That was it," said a floor broker of the move on the Yeltsin rumor and denial. "People got hung out to dry today on that rumor because they flocked to the safe-haven Swiss and then it came back off."

The Swiss unit had broken late Tuesday and further on Wednesday after Swiss National Bank council member Bruno Gehrig said the Swiss unit had not yet fully reflected the effect of the recent Swiss rate cut.
Technically, some chartists looked for Swiss to fall soon. "I do agree the Swiss is a bit toppish and has more downside," said a broker, who pegged a target of $0.7900 within a month.

Yen had stopped falling overnight when Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of Japan's Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, called "groundless" a rumor that U.S. officials had said they would tolerate the dollar at 120 yen.

The mark stayed under pressure on European economic and monetary union convergence talk and vague rumors that Thursday's Bundesbank council meeting might yield a rate cut, although most doubted the German central bank would ease.
After the close, Canadian finance minister Paul Martin began delivering his autumn budget assessment. August Canadian employment figures are due on Friday.

December yen ended off $0.000015 at $0.009041, marks eased $0.0004 to $0.6570, Swiss francs lost $0.0025 to $0.8032, Sterling gained $0.0022 to $1.5640, Canadian dollar rose $0.0003 to $0.7412, Aussie dollar eased $0.0002 to $0.7885, Mexican peso fell $0.000500 to $0.126850. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
